identity.title: Position: AI Competitions Provide the Gold Standard for Empirical Rigor in GenAI Evaluation

problem.claim: GenAI evaluation faces challenges from typically nearly unbounded input/output spaces, unclear ground truth, feedback loops, context-dependent predictions, leakage, and contamination.

gap.claim: Traditional ML evaluation and benchmarking are described as insufficient for modern GenAI, while AI Competitions’ relevant practices remain underutilized.

contributions.claim: Argues that AI Competitions should serve as a gold standard for empirical rigor in GenAI evaluation.
Identifies leakage and contamination as the most important and difficult GenAI evaluation issues to address.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that AI Competitions have developed effective anti-leakage measures and practices to counter cheating in competition settings.
The authors report that these competition practices constitute an especially valuable but underutilized resource for GenAI evaluation.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper characterizes GenAI empirical evaluation as being in crisis because traditional evaluation and benchmarking strategies are insufficient.
It attributes the difficulty to open-ended spaces, weakly defined targets, feedback loops, and context-dependent prediction.
It presents leakage and contamination as the most important and difficult issues to address.
It points to AI Competitions’ anti-leakage practices and calls for treating competitions as a gold standard and using their results accordingly.

source_observation.claim: The abstract isolates leakage and contamination as priority problems, then connects them to concrete anti-cheating practices developed in AI Competitions.

lessons.interpretation: A persuasive position can align a prioritized failure mode with an existing practice that directly targets it.
lessons.application: When proposing an evaluation framework, name the dominant threat explicitly and map it to an established mitigation procedure or resource.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when the proposed threat or mitigation does not match the evaluation setting’s data-generation and feedback dynamics.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify which competition measures, datasets, models, or evaluation results support the gold-standard claim.
It does not establish that competition practices transfer successfully to all GenAI evaluation settings.

editorial_revisions.after: GenAI evaluation faces challenges from typically nearly unbounded input/output spaces, unclear ground truth, feedback loops, context-dependent predictions, leakage, and contamination.
